messages:
Tessa: Hey team, multiple APAC customers reporting p99 token latency spikes ~2.5-3s starting ~08:12 UTC. Happening intermittently for generation requests. Example trace id: trace-APAC-9a7f. Not seeing errors, just slow tails. Can we triage?
Samir: looking — can you paste a couple of raw request headers + x-request-id/trace header from affected requests? Also which endpoint (host) and model?
Tessa: sending one from customer A:
```
:method: POST
:authority: api.redwood.example
:path: /v1/generate
model: redwood-alpha-7b
x-request-id: r-a1b2c3
x-trace-id: trace-APAC-9a7f
x-customer-region: ap-south1
```
Samir: thanks. Two quick asks: 1) are these using our hosted API (yes), 2) did they have region affinity pinned?
Tessa: they did not set affinity, relying on our auto-routing.
Jordan: can you run a tracewalk or traceroute for one of the slow requests? Preferably the trace logs produced by our egress tracer. Any span showing region handoff?
Tessa: attached the tracer we get from the request (extract):
```
span0: client->edge ap-south1 (lat 30ms)
span1: edge ap-south1 -> us-east-1 (lat 200ms)
span2: us-east-1 -> ap-south1 (lat 220ms)
span3: ap-south1->compute (lat 25ms)
```
Tessa: so looks like a detour to us-east then back to ap-south1. Customers see the extra ~400ms loop.
Priya: that matches what I feared — some host routes were preferring a shared backbone path that transits us-east for a subset of edges. Can you share the edge node id?
Tessa: edge id: edge-ap-9. Happening across ~10% of their requests.
infra-bot: Canary rollout event: dedicated-edge-routing v4.12 -> rolled to 12% of APAC edges at 08:10 UTC (change-id: canary-2026-8472).
Jordan: ah — canary changed route preferences. It probably introduced a path preference that prefers an intermediate transit in us-east for that edge. Priya, can you check the route preference table for canary-2026-8472 vs v4.11?
Priya: checking... quick diff: v4.12 introduced BGP prepends for ap-south1->global that inadvertently lowered local preference, causing some AS paths to prefer exit toward us-east before re-entering AP. Repro steps: deploy canary, run `traceroute -T api.redwood.example` from edge-ap-9 and inspect next-hop AS.
Samir: mitigation options while we fix config: 1) roll back canary on impacted edges, 2) set a temporary routing override to prefer local egress for ap-south1, 3) advise customer to set region-affinity header `X-Redwood-Region: ap-south1` to avoid cross-region routing (works as a short term).
Tessa: can we do quick rollback? Customers asking for ETA.
Jordan: I'm patching the rollout to remove ap-south1 from canary cohort and forcing v4.11 on those edges. Rolling now.
infra-bot: Rollback initiated (change-id: canary-2026-8472) — 12% -> 0% for APAC cohort at 08:24 UTC.
Samir: after rollback, please capture new traces.
Tessa: new trace for a previously slow request:
```
span0: client->edge ap-south1 (lat 28ms)
span1: edge ap-south1->compute (lat 22ms)
```
Tessa: p99 for that customer dropped back under 300ms. Confirmed by customer on support call. :tada:
Jordan: we'll revert the BGP prepends and vet the prepends in staging with an AS-path simulator before reattempting. Also adding a guardrail: any routing change that increases cross-region path length for >5% of a region's edges must be blocked from canary.
Priya: noted. I'll post the staged test plan and the AS-path diff.
Samir: action items: Priya to post config diff + test plan, Jordan to validate rollback and add canary guardrail, Samir to update customer thread with mitigation steps and ask them to use `X-Redwood-Region` if they need immediate hard affinity.
Tessa: thanks all. Will update customer with rollback + ETA for permanent fix.
Jordan: FYI we'll also add a tracing alert rule to fire if any single request shows >1 cross-region hop in trace path for a region more than 1% of traffic. That should catch regressions earlier.
Tessa: appreciated. Closing from our side if no regressions after 1 hour.
Samir: closing — will reopen if we see reoccurrence.
infra-bot: Monitoring note: p99 APAC egress latency back to baseline at 08:29 UTC.
